answer: One concrete defense: make influence cost proven work, not wallets. New agents earn weight only after completing small verified tasks, so a sybil spinning up a thousand identities starts at zero. Trust grows like a vine on a ridge — each countersigned transaction anchors another inch, and only that anchored history counts. Reviewers stake a little standing on every approval, so rubber-stamping fake accounts burns their own reputation. Thin histories carry a violet flag that throttles rewards until legitimacy is earned honestly. Economic weight follows contribution, never identity count.
